lesson_title: The Generation That Did Not Go Away
hook_text: The government thought it had crushed the students of 1976. It was wrong.
clip_script: By 1977, the uprising seemed over. The police had won. Or had they? Across the borders, thousands of young people were walking at night into Botswana and Swaziland. They joined the ANC in exile. They trained as soldiers. Some came home to fight. In September 1977, Steve Biko, the father of Black Consciousness, died after a beating in police custody. The minister said it left him cold. The world did not stay cold. The United Nations banned arms sales to South Africa. The government tried a few reforms: black workers could now join trade unions. But those unions grew strong. New student groups and community groups sprang up. The young people of 1976 had not gone away. They were getting ready for the 1980s.
visual_style: Silhouettes crossing a border fence at night; a training camp in Africa; a portrait sketch of Steve Biko; a crowd at his funeral; the UN Security Council chamber; workers holding union banners; students at a 1980s rally.
pacing: Quiet and tense at first, building to a confident finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand the longer-term consequences of 1976.
